name: Auto-reply to Rightmove and Zoopla property enquiries with GPT-4o, Gmail and Google Sheets

parameters.content:
## Auto-reply to Rightmove and Zoopla property enquiries with GPT-4o, Gmail and Google Sheets

**Who it's for:** letting agents and property teams handling portal enquiries by hand.

**The problem it solves:** portal leads go cold in minutes — the first agency to reply properly usually wins the tenant, but staff reply hours later and often re-ask questions the applicant already answered on the portal. This workflow replies in under a minute, personalised, with staff still in control.

### How it works

The Gmail trigger watches the inbox for new enquiries, the classifier identifies which portal each one came from (Rightmove, Zoopla, OnTheMarket, SpareRoom or a website form) and drops portal admin email. GPT-4o extracts the enquirer's details and qualification data (employment, affordability, move-in date, pets and more), the enquiry is matched to a property in your Google Sheet, and a personalised reply is drafted that never re-asks a question the applicant has already answered. The reply carries a pre-qualification form button, or offers similar available properties when the one they asked about has been let. Every enquiry is logged to the sheet. By default every reply is created as a Gmail draft, threaded to the enquiry, for staff approval; an optional auto-send mode replies automatically to safe, fresh enquiries and marks them read. An optional WhatsApp branch sends the form link to enquirers who left a phone number.

### Setup steps

- Connect a Gmail OAuth2 credential on the four Gmail nodes (trigger, draft, reply, mark as read).
- Connect your OpenAI credential on both model nodes.
- Create a Google Sheet with two tabs — **Properties** (headers: `ref`, `address`, `rent`, `bedrooms`, `available_from`, `status`, `area`, `notes`) and **Enquiry Log** (headers: `source`, `received_at`, `enquirer_name`, `email`, `phone`, `property_address`, `property_ref`, `property_rent`, `cta`, `outcome`, `subject`) — and select it in both Sheets nodes.
- In *Match Property and Build Links*, set your agency name, pre-qualification form URL and the auto-send switch.
- In *Build Branded Email*, set your brand colour, sign-off, phone, website, office address and legal footer.
- Optional: configure the WhatsApp nodes with your Cloud API phone number ID and approved template, or delete them.
- Test safely with the manual trigger — it feeds a fake enquiry through the full pipeline without touching real email.

### Customization

Adjust the enquiry sources, extraction fields, qualification checklist, reply tone and structure in the system prompt, branding, auto-send rules and sheet columns to fit your team's process.

## Watch the inbox

The native Gmail trigger checks for new unread mail every minute and hands each message on, already parsed and deduplicated.

## Classify and extract

Identifies which portal the enquiry came from and drops portal admin email. GPT-4o then extracts contact details and qualification data into a structured record.

## Match the property

The enquiry is matched to a row in your Properties tab by reference or address. Availability and similar-property suggestions come from the sheet's status column.

## Draft the reply

GPT-4o writes a personalised reply that acknowledges what the applicant already told us and never re-asks it. The branded HTML wrapper adds the form button, similar-property cards and your signature.

## Log every enquiry

Every enquiry lands in the Enquiry Log tab with its outcome, whether or not a reply was drafted.

## Deliver: draft for approval, or auto-send

By default every reply becomes a Gmail draft, threaded to the original enquiry, for staff to review and send. When auto-send is enabled in *Match Property and Build Links*, safe form replies to fresh enquiries are sent as a native Gmail reply and the original message is marked read.

## Optional: WhatsApp follow-up

Sends your approved WhatsApp template with the form link to enquirers who left a phone number. Requires the Meta WhatsApp Cloud API. Delete both nodes if you don't use WhatsApp.

## Test without emailing

The manual trigger feeds a fake enquiry through the whole pipeline. Edit the test data to match a row in your Properties tab and try different scenarios.

options.systemPromptTemplate:
You extract structured lettings enquiry data from emails received by a UK letting agent.

RULES:
- Extract ONLY what is explicitly present in the email. Never guess, infer or invent a value.
- If a field is not present, return null. Do not substitute a placeholder.
- Keep values close to the source wording (e.g. "Household income exceeds £24,000", "Within 1 month").
- Some enquiries arrive as a narrative summary rather than labelled fields — read it carefully and pull out the facts stated there.
- phone: keep the number as written; do not reformat.
- OnTheMarket emails: the enquirer's OWN home is under 'Address'; the property they're enquiring about is under 'PropAddress' and 'Your agency ref' (e.g. 10822). Use the property (PropAddress + the agency ref) for property_address and property_ref — never the enquirer's own Address.
- viewing_requested: true only if the enquirer clearly asks to view / arrange a viewing.
- enquiry_intent: classify why the caller contacted us, choosing the closest of new_let_enquiry / existing_customer / cancellation / other. This one field is a classification, not a copied fact, so pick the best-fitting category from the summary.

parameters.inputSchema:
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "enquirer_name":     { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Full name of the person enquiring" },
    "email":             { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Enquirer email address" },
    "phone":             { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Enquirer phone number" },
    "property_address":  { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Full property address as shown" },
    "property_ref":      { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Agent property reference, e.g. AB1234 or 10432" },
    "property_price":    { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Advertised rent, e.g. £950 pcm" },
    "enquiry_message":   { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Free-text message written by the enquirer" },
    "moving_date":       { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "When they want to move, e.g. Within 1 month" },
    "tenancy_duration":  { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Desired tenancy length, e.g. 6 months" },
    "moving_with":       { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Who they are moving with, e.g. Myself, Family" },
    "occupants":         { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Number of occupants if stated" },
    "pets":              { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Yes / No / null" },
    "smokers":           { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Yes / No / null" },
    "first_time_renter": { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Yes / No / null" },
    "employment":        { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Employment status, e.g. Full time employed" },
    "affordability":     { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Stated income or affordability, e.g. Household income exceeds £24,000" },
    "guarantor":         { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Guarantor info if stated" },
    "adverse_credit":    { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Adverse credit info, e.g. Not aware" },
    "parking_required":  { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Whether parking is needed, if mentioned" },
    "applicant_wants":   { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "What the applicant asked for, e.g. More details on this property, a viewing" },
    "viewing_requested": { "type": ["boolean"], "description": "True if they explicitly asked to view the property" },
    "enquiry_intent":    { "type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Classify the enquirer's purpose: 'new_let_enquiry' (asking about renting or viewing a property available to let), 'existing_customer' (already a tenant or part-way through an application — rent payment, references, repairs, portal access, complaint), 'cancellation' (cancelling or rescheduling an existing viewing/appointment), or 'other' (valuation, sales, or a general question). For Rightmove, Zoopla and website enquiries this is always 'new_let_enquiry'." }
  },
  "required": ["enquirer_name", "viewing_requested"]
}

messageValues.message:
You are writing on behalf of the letting agency named under "Agency" in the enquiry details — a UK letting agent. You draft the reply to a new rental enquiry. A member of staff will usually review your draft before it is sent, so write it as a finished email, ready to go.

HOUSE STYLE
- Warm, professional, plain British English. Never American spelling.
- Short paragraphs. No corporate waffle, no exclamation marks, no emoji.
- Address the person by first name.
- Never invent facts about the property (availability, bills, deposit, parking). If you do not know, do not say it.

THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT RULE
Never ask the applicant a question they have already answered. Read "WHAT WE ALREADY KNOW ABOUT THEM" carefully. If their employment, income, credit position, move-in date or pet status is listed there, do NOT ask for it again — instead, briefly acknowledge it so they feel heard.

STRUCTURE
1. Thank them for their enquiry and name the property.
2. If they asked a specific question in their message, answer it if you can — or say a colleague will confirm shortly. Never bluff.
3. Bridge to the next step: to arrange a viewing, the agency first needs a few details to check suitability.
4. Give the pre-qualification form as the clear call to action. It takes a couple of minutes and means a viewing can be booked quickly.
5. If anything is listed under "STILL MISSING" that the form does not obviously cover, you may ask for it — but keep it to a maximum of two questions, and only if genuinely needed.
6. Close warmly, inviting them to reply with any questions.

SOURCE-SPECIFIC GUIDANCE
- If source is "rightmove": they have already supplied most of their details. Acknowledge that ("thanks for the details you've already provided"), ask nothing further, and go straight to the form.
- If source is "zoopla", "onthemarket", "spareroom" or "website": no details supplied yet, so the pre-qualification form IS the ask. Keep it friendly and light.

IMPORTANT - do NOT add any of the following (they are added automatically): a sign-off or closing such as 'Kind regards' / 'Best regards' / a team name; a name or job title; the pre-qualification link, a URL, or a 'click here'/'form below' label. End your message at the last sentence of the body. Refer to the form naturally (e.g. 'complete our quick pre-qualification form') without a link.

CALL TO ACTION (this rule is authoritative and OVERRIDES any instruction above about the form, link or button)
Use the "CTA" value in the inputs to decide how to close:
- CTA = form: invite them to complete the quick pre-qualification form (a button is added automatically after your message - do NOT paste a link or a URL).
- CTA = alternatives: the property they asked about has just been let. Warmly tell them so, then point them to a few similar available properties shown just below your message (cards are added automatically - do NOT list the addresses or links yourself). Invite them to reply if they would like to view any of them.
- CTA = none: there is NO form or link for this enquiry - do NOT mention, promise or imply one. If "Still available" is false, warmly say that property has just been let and invite them to reply telling us what they are looking for so we can help. Otherwise thank them and say a colleague will follow up shortly with the next steps. Keep it warm and brief.
